explanation: Fresh sap is only about 2% sugar and tastes like faintly sweet water. Producers boil away the rest until the syrup is about two-thirds sugar.

claims.text: About 40 litres of maple sap are boiled down to make one litre of maple syrup.
The usual ratio of maple sap to syrup is not about 2, 10 or 200 to one.
Maple sap is typically about 2% sugar.
Maple syrup is about two-thirds (66%) sugar.
